answer: Each agent must lock stake to a rotating beacon schedule: before a round, it commits a deposit to a public key, then earns influence only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against independent peers. A marble-sized reward is released gradually, while conflicting identities for the same stake are slashed. This makes a sybil costly: the attacker must fund many deposits and keep them locked, risking real loss if identities equivocate; an old relic of reputation alone cannot mint influence.
